explanations: terra: Those killed in God's path must not be called dead; the correction supplies the life beyond death assumed when martyrdom is named a good outcome.

luna: The verse joins giving wealth, fulfilling covenants, and patience in hardship and at battle; it gathers the source section's gift, fidelity, and sustained combat into one account of righteousness. | terra: Giving wealth, keeping a covenant, and patience حِينَ ٱلْبَأْسِ culminate in أُولَٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا۟; the ayah directly makes truth the completion of costly action, as the section's sound charge does.

terra: The command to fight continues until persecution ends, then orders hostilities to cease if the opponents stop; it gives both an endpoint for sustained combat and a boundary against needless continuation.
terra: Spending in God's way appears inside the fighting passage and is joined to the warning not to cast oneself into ruin; giving supports the campaign while remaining governed by right action.
terra: Fighting is prescribed though disliked, and what is disliked may be good; the ayah warns that aversion at the outset does not determine the charge's true outcome.
terra: The command to fight in God's way immediately precedes the call to lend God a good loan in 2:245, placing combat and giving side by side.
terra: The good loan to God follows the command to fight in 2:244; the adjacency makes material giving part of answering the martial summons.

luna: When fighting is prescribed, most of the Israelites turn away except a few; the ayah is a direct Quranic example of a call to fight broken off before the charge. | terra: Those who asked for a king so they could fight then تَوَلَّوْا۟ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا when fighting was prescribed; intention collapses before execution in the section's precise sense of an aborted charge.

terra: After the river test, some say they have no power against Goliath, while those expecting to meet God answer that a small steadfast force can defeat a large one; one army divides into faltering and sustained resolve.

luna: Facing Goliath's army, the believers ask Allah to pour patience on them and make their feet firm; it gives the section's steadfast battle effort a specific prayer. | terra: Facing Goliath, the faithful ask for poured-out patience and firm feet before seeking victory; the prayer articulates what lets the charge reach its end.

luna: The next ayah records David killing Goliath and the opposing force being defeated by Allah's permission; it supplies victory as the result of the stand prayed for in 2:250. | terra: They defeat the enemy by God's permission and David kills Goliath; it supplies the completed victory sought in 2:250 and contrasts the collapse voiced in 2:249.

luna: At Uhud, two groups among the believers were close to losing heart (تَفْشَلَا), though Allah was their protector; it shows a near-break in the charge that stopped short of the flight in the source image. | terra: Two groups nearly lose courage even though God is their protector; the near-failure marks the threshold between a charge sustained by trust and one abandoned.
terra: وَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ forbids weakness after battle and promises the believers the upper position; it is a direct command not to let the charge collapse.
luna: After Uhud, fortunes alternate and Allah takes martyrs from among the believers; this gives the section's shahada outcome a concrete place within a changing battle.
luna: The verse says Allah purifies believers and effaces disbelievers in the continuing Uhud scene; it names a further consequence of the battle that produces the martyrs in 3:140.
luna: The verse asks whether believers expect Paradise before Allah distinguishes those who strive and remain patient; it makes sustained effort in battle the test behind the section's good outcome.

luna: The verse recalls that believers had wished for death before meeting it and then saw it; it gives the section's martyr outcome the moment of facing battle death. | terra: Believers had wished for death before meeting it and are reminded that they have now seen it; the ayah tests a prior declaration at the moment when battlefield action must substantiate it.

luna: The verse asks whether believers would turn back if Muhammad died or were killed; it connects back-turning to fear of loss in battle and says it cannot harm Allah. | terra: The question أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ makes turning on one's heels after the leader's loss the reversal of faithful persistence.

luna: The verse recalls fighters beside prophets who did not weaken or submit after hardship; it shows the sustained resolve opposite the section's abandoned charge. | terra: Those fighting with prophets neither lost heart, weakened, nor yielded; the triple negation gives the sustained combat denoted by the section's صدق branch.
terra: The fighters' prayer وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا asks for firm feet before victory, giving bodily language to the section's refusal to turn and flee.
terra: Obeying the disbelievers would يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ, making reversal on one's heels the loss that follows abandoned fidelity.

luna: At Uhud the verse says Allah fulfilled His promise (the source section's root ص د ق) until the believers faltered, disputed, and disobeyed; it stages fulfilled resolve followed by a broken battle effort. | terra: God had صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ while they struck the enemy, until courage failed, dispute arose, and they disobeyed; the ayah places fulfilled truth and an interrupted attack on opposite sides of one battle.

luna: The Uhud scene shows believers climbing without looking back while the Messenger calls them from behind; this supplies a literal battlefield back-turning and its immediate grief. | terra: At Uhud the believers climb away, heed no one, and leave the Messenger calling from behind; the ayah makes battlefield flight visible after the failure described in 3:152.

luna: At Uhud some turned back when the armies met, yet Allah pardoned them; this marks a boundary between a battle retreat and the source section's denier who turns away toward fire. | terra: Those who تَوَلَّوْا۟ on the day the armies met were made to slip through some of what they had earned; the root names an actual battlefield withdrawal.

luna: The verse says death in Allah's cause brings forgiveness and mercy better than what people gather; this gives the section's martyrdom outcome a reward that outweighs worldly goods. | terra: Being killed or dying in God's path leads to forgiveness and mercy better than accumulated goods; it explains the value assigned to the death side of the section's two fair outcomes.

terra: After Uhud, gentleness keeps followers gathered whereas harshness would disperse them; consultation is followed by firm resolve and trust, showing that softness of manner can enable decisive action.

luna: Invited to fight or defend, the hypocrites say they would follow if they knew how to fight, then are described as speaking what is not in their hearts; this is a battle-specific gap between claim and action. | terra: Called to fight or at least defend, the hypocrites excuse themselves and say with their mouths what is not in their hearts; the war setting exposes untrue speech through refusal to act.

luna: Those who stayed behind claim their advice would have prevented their brothers' deaths; the verse challenges them to repel death if they are truthful (صَادِقِينَ), joining the source root ص د ق to the battle's two outcomes. | terra: Those who sat back claim their slain brothers would have lived had they obeyed; إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ challenges them to repel death themselves, turning claimed truth against battlefield avoidance.

luna: The verse says those killed in Allah's cause are alive and provided for; it explains the martyr side of the section's two good outcomes beyond the battlefield. | terra: Those killed in God's path are alive and provided for with their Lord; the ayah explains why martyrdom can be one of the section's two fair battlefield outcomes.

luna: The next ayah after the martyrs are called alive and provided for says they rejoice in Allah's bounty and have no fear; it expands the section's shahada outcome into joy without fear. | terra: The slain rejoice in God's bounty and in those who have not yet joined them, with no fear or grief; this continues 3:169 by showing martyrdom as a genuinely favorable outcome.

luna: The following ayah says the martyrs rejoice in Allah's grace and that He does not waste the believers' reward; it completes the post-battle reward passage begun in 3:169. | terra: The martyrs rejoice in divine favor and reward, completing the passage's account of why battlefield death belongs among the good outcomes.

luna: After being wounded, believers answer Allah and the Messenger's call to pursue; this is a specific case of resuming the effort after pain, with a great reward promised to those who do good and fear God. | terra: Despite wounds, the believers respond to God and the Messenger; renewed action after injury is a particularly concrete instance of carrying the campaign through.

luna: The warning that an enemy force had gathered only increases believers' faith and reliance; this neighboring ayah adds their response to intimidation after they had answered the call in 3:172. | terra: News that a force had gathered against them increases the wounded believers' faith rather than turning them back, showing resolve strengthened at the threat of renewed combat.

luna: The next ayah says they returned with grace and bounty and no harm touched them; it adds an uninjured return as the outcome of the pursuit in 3:172. | terra: They return with divine favor, untouched by harm, after following God's pleasure; the return supplies the favorable outcome of the response in 3:172-173.

luna: The verse remembers believers driven from home, harmed, then fighting and being killed; it links hardship, a completed fight, and divine reward to the section's martyr outcome. | terra: Male and female are made reciprocal, then exile, injury, fighting, and death receive promised gardens; this ayah brings the section's sex pair directly into its battlefield and martyrdom outcome.
terra: ٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلْجَنۢبِ names the companion at one's side; that spatial sense directly explains the dictionary statement that a shield is called مِجْنَب because it stays beside the person.
terra: Believers must take precautions and advance in detachments or all together; organized readiness supplies the practical protective side of the section's shield and assault.

luna: The verse says a fighter may be killed or prevail, and either way receives a great reward; it gives the section's victory-or-martyrdom gloss of الْحُسْنَىٰ a direct battle setting. | terra: The fighter may be killed or prevail, فَيُقْتَلْ أَوْ يَغْلِبْ, and receives immense reward in either case; it spells out the two good ends compressed into ٱلْحُسْنَيَيْنِ.
terra: When fighting is prescribed, a group fears people as God should be feared and asks for delay; the verse stages resolve collapsing precisely when combat becomes obligatory.
luna: The verse records people saying “obedience” and then plotting otherwise; in the passage framed by the command to fight at 4:77, it states the source section's speech-versus-action divide.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to fight even though accountable only for himself and to urge the believers; personal resolve carries the summons forward despite uncertain support.

luna: The verse distinguishes those who sit from those who strive with wealth and lives, while promising good to both and greater rank to the fighters; it clarifies the different weight of entering the struggle. | terra: The ayah distinguishes uninjured sitters from those striving with wealth and lives and gives the latter higher rank; it makes enacted commitment, rather than a claim to belief, the boundary.

luna: While one group prays under threat, it must keep its arms (أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ) ready and the other group takes its turn; this parallels the section's weapons-and-shield image without claiming the verse names a shield. | terra: In danger prayer one company stands while taking its weapons, then another replaces it with precautions and arms; the alternating armed groups echo the section's weapon passed between hands, although no transfer is stated.

luna: The verse tells believers not to weaken in pursuing the enemy; even if they suffer, the enemy suffers too, while they hope in Allah, extending the section's charge through hardship. | terra: وَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ فِى ٱبْتِغَآءِ ٱلْقَوْمِ forbids weakening in pursuit despite shared pain, making perseverance the distinguishing feature of the attack.

terra: Whoever does righteous deeds, male or female, enters the Garden without injustice; the ayah blocks the weapon lexicon's male/strong and female/weak labels from becoming a scale of human efficacy.
terra: Moses orders his people to enter and وَلَا تَرْتَدُّوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِكُمْ; the warning makes back-turning the act that converts a commanded advance into loss.
terra: Two Godfearing men command ٱدْخُلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْبَابَ and promise victory once the entry is made; it is the advance the larger people refuse in 5:24.

luna: The Israelites tell Moses to go fight while they remain seated (إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَاعِدُونَ); this is a direct refusal to enter the battle that contrasts with the section's fighter who completes a charge. | terra: فَٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ is the blunt reversal of a sound charge: the addressees leave fighting to others and announce that they will sit.

luna: By analogy only, the verse pairs humility toward believers with might toward disbelievers and explicitly mentions fighting; its directed qualities resemble the section's hard and yielding iron, though it describes people rather than weapons. | terra: The divinely loved people are humble toward believers, mighty toward unbelievers, and strive without fearing blame; like 48:29, the ayah assigns softness and hardness to their proper relations while retaining courage in action.

luna: The source dictionary form is رُمْحٌ صِدْقٌ, a sound spear; 5:94 names spears (رِمَاحُكُمْ) in a hunting test, not a battle. This limited boundary reading shows the weapon's force held back where restraint is required. | terra: Game within reach of أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ places the spear in an actual striking scene, giving a Quranic object for the dictionary's رُمْحٌ صِدْقٌ, though the context is a test during pilgrimage rather than war.

luna: The battle command to strike above the necks and at fingertips gives the section's cutting sword a direct Quranic combat scene. | terra: The battlefield command to strike above necks and every fingertip supplies an explicit cutting-weapon action for the section's effective sword.

luna: The command not to turn backs when facing an enemy is the direct battlefield boundary against the back-turning in the source section. | terra: At the moment of meeting an advancing enemy, فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ ٱلْأَدْبَارَ expressly forbids the battlefield back-turning heard in the section's وَلَّىٰ هَارِبًا.

luna: This ayah condemns turning one's back in battle but exempts a tactical maneuver or joining another group; it gives the section's fleeing image both its limit and its grave consequence. | terra: Whoever يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ دُبُرَهُ without a tactical exception incurs wrath and Hell; it supplies the destination of the retreat forbidden in 8:15 and mirrored by the source fire.

luna: At Badr, the verse says the Prophet did not throw when he threw, but Allah threw; this qualifies the section's image of a completed human charge by locating the battle's effect under divine action.

luna: Disbelievers spend wealth to block Allah's path, are then defeated, and are gathered to Hell; this reverses the section's giving for a good battle outcome into expenditure that fails and ends in Fire.

luna: At meeting an enemy force, the verse commands believers to stand firm (فَاثْبُتُوا۟); this is the military steadiness behind the section's sound spear and charge carried through. | terra: When believers meet a force, فَٱثْبُتُوا۟ commands them to stand firm; it is the positive battlefield act opposed to breaking off a charge.

luna: The verse warns that dispute makes a fighting group fail and lose its force; its neighbor 8:45 commands firmness, while this ayah names what breaks it. | terra: Dispute would make believers fail and lose their force, so they must be patient; the ayah identifies the internal fracture that turns a firm line into a failed assault.

luna: Satan promises support when the armies are apart, but when they meet he turns back on his heels (نَكَصَ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ); it is a precise battle image of assurance abandoned at the charge. | terra: Satan first guarantees victory, but when the two forces appear نَكَصَ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ; assurance turns into a literal retreat at contact, embodying the section's charge that fails midway.
luna: The verse describes people who break covenants repeatedly and then addresses meeting them in war; it contrasts broken pledges with the source section's ص د ق as fulfilled combat effort.

luna: The command to prepare whatever force and cavalry can be mustered is a direct Quranic counterpart to the section's bow, spear, and sword as battle equipment. | terra: Preparing all available force and tethered horses turns readiness into deterrent power; it supplies the organized martial preparation presupposed by a firm charge.
terra: If the enemy inclines to peace, the Prophet must incline to it; this sets an explicit divine boundary on the section's image of carrying an assault to completion.

luna: The command to urge believers to fight and the promise that a small patient group can face a larger one make endurance in battle explicit. | terra: The Prophet must urge believers to fight, and twenty patient fighters may overcome two hundred; patience supplies the human firmness behind the section's solid weapon.

luna: The next ayah eases the ratio because of weakness while retaining the command to endure; it marks a limit to the firmness demanded in 8:65. | terra: God acknowledges فِيكُمْ ضَعْفًۭا and reduces the ratio while still requiring patient resistance; the ayah distinguishes real weakness from simply abandoning combat.
terra: Emigrants who strive with wealth and lives become mutual protectors with those who shelter and aid them; giving, combat commitment, and protection converge in one ayah.
terra: Those who migrate, strive, shelter, and aid are called true believers and promised forgiveness and noble provision; completed support and struggle establish the claim to faith.
terra: Those who believe, migrate, and strive with wealth and lives receive the greater rank; expenditure and completed struggle again stand as one enacted commitment.
terra: Family, property, trade, and homes must not be dearer than God, His Messenger, and striving; cherished possessions become the concrete test of whether giving and advance will be completed.

luna: At Hunayn, believers turned their backs after being impressed by their numbers; this is a concrete battle retreat, distinct from the denier's turn in the source section. | terra: At Hunayn numerical confidence failed and ثُمَّ وَلَّيْتُم مُّدْبِرِينَ; the ayah shows a strong-looking force reversing direction under pressure.
luna: After the retreat in 9:25, Allah sent tranquility upon the Messenger and believers; the neighboring ayah adds restoration after flight and prevents treating every retreat as the same case.
terra: Asked to march, believers are reproached for clinging heavily to the earth; bodily heaviness becomes the contrary image to a charge brought fully forward.

luna: The command to march and strive with wealth and lives makes the section's gift and battle effort one joined act. | terra: The command to go forth light or heavy and strive with wealth and lives fuses material giving with refusal to let difficulty halt the campaign.
terra: Those deterred by distance swear they would have marched if able, but God knows إِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ; campaign refusal gives their lie its enacted meaning.

terra: The Prophet's permission delayed disclosure of those who spoke truth and the liars among campaign excuse-makers; 9:42 supplies the false oath and avoided march that give this test its concrete content.

luna: The verse says true believers do not ask to stay behind from striving with wealth and lives; it contrasts the source section's steadfast giver with those who hold back. | terra: Those who truly believe do not ask exemption from striving with wealth and lives; refusal to seek escape makes action the evidence of their faith.
terra: Those who ask exemption are the doubters whose hearts waver; their hesitation supplies the opposite of the truthful fighter's settled charge.
terra: Had they intended to go out they would have prepared, but they were held back and told to sit; lack of preparation exposes a professed campaign as an action never carried through.
luna: The opponents are distressed by a good outcome and rejoice at misfortune, then turn away (يَتَوَلَّوا۟); the neighboring 9:52 answers them that believers face only two good battle outcomes.
luna: This ayah says nothing will strike believers except what Allah has decreed and calls them to rely on Him; the next 9:52 names victory or martyrdom as the battle's two goods.

luna: The section's dictionary gloss for الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ is victory or martyrdom; this battle challenge names precisely the two outcomes the hostile waiters must expect. | terra: The commanded challenge إِلَّآ إِحْدَى ٱلْحُسْنَيَيْنِ names the section's two fair battlefield outcomes, victory or martyrdom, as all believers await for themselves.
terra: Voluntary or unwilling spending will not be accepted from the defiantly disobedient; the ayah separates the bare transfer of wealth from the truthful giving represented in the section.
terra: Their expenditures fail because they disbelieve, approach prayer lazily, and spend reluctantly; incomplete inward assent makes the outward gift ineffective.
terra: Hypocritical men and women belong to one another, command wrong, and close their hands; the paired sexes share the withholding action that opposes the source giver.
terra: Believing men and women are allies who command right and give alms; the same paired sexes share active giving and mutual protection, reversing 9:67's closed hands.
terra: The pledge لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ promises that a divine gift will be answered by giving; 9:76-77 show that refusing to complete it turns the promised charity into a lie.
terra: After God gives them bounty, بَخِلُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَتَوَلَّوا۟; stinginess and turning away fuse the section's ungiving man with its retreating fighter.
terra: The broken promise of 9:75-76 ends بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ, defining lying as failure to carry a pledged act through rather than as words alone.

luna: The people left behind rejoice at staying home and dislike striving with wealth and lives; this is the refusal to enter the campaign that precedes the section's image of a charge abandoned. | terra: The ones left behind rejoice in sitting and dislike striving with wealth and lives; their settled refusal reverses the section's giver who completes the attack.

luna: After the people who stayed behind disliked the campaign in 9:81, this ayah says they will not be allowed to go out or fight alongside the Messenger again; it gives refusal a concrete consequence. | terra: Because they accepted sitting the first time, the laggards are told they will never again go out or fight with the Prophet; initial withdrawal becomes exclusion from the completed campaign.
terra: When revelation commands belief and striving beside the Messenger, the affluent ask leave to remain behind; capacity without action exposes the abandoned summons.
terra: They are content to remain with those left behind, so their hearts are sealed; this gives the settled posture of the refusal voiced in 9:86.
terra: The Messenger and believers strive with wealth and lives and receive ٱلْخَيْرَٰتُ; their enacted giving and combat form the positive counterpart to the sitters of the passage.
terra: Excuse-makers seek permission while those who كَذَبُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ sit back; lying is concretely manifested as absence from the campaign.
terra: The weak, ill, and genuinely unequipped incur no blame when sincere; this distinguishes inability from the moral failure of a capable person who breaks off or avoids the charge.
terra: Those turned away only because no mount could be found leave with eyes overflowing in grief; their frustrated desire to contribute forms the clearest boundary against cowardly retreat.
terra: Blame falls on the wealthy who ask permission and accept remaining behind; ample capacity makes their refusal the inverse of complete giving and action.

luna: The verse binds wealth and lives to fighting and says believers may kill or be killed, in exchange for Paradise; it joins the section's giving and completed charge to the two good battle outcomes. | terra: Believers spend both property and life, fight, kill and are killed, under a true promise whose fulfillment none exceeds; the ayah unites giving, full combat, martyrdom, and completed truth.

terra: During the Hour of Hardship some hearts nearly swerved, yet God turned to the Prophet, emigrants, and helpers who followed him; the near-defection and preserved following illuminate a campaign carried through strain.

luna: The three left behind from Tabuk are eventually forgiven after recognizing they had no refuge from Allah; this is a specific case of repentance after staying behind, unlike the source section's denier who turns toward Fire. | terra: The three left behind endure constriction until they know there is no refuge from God except with Him, and God turns to them; their truthful repentance marks recovery after failure to join the campaign.

luna: Following the account of those left behind, this ayah commands believers to be with the truthful (الصَّادِقِينَ); it brings the source root ص د ق into the same campaign's question of who truly follows through. | terra: After the hardship and the three left behind in 9:117-118, believers are commanded to fear God and be with the truthful; campaign conduct gives the command its concrete setting.

luna: The verse says Medina's people and nearby Arabs should not stay behind the Messenger or prefer their own lives over his; it directly opposes the section's retreating fighter and self-protective stance. | terra: Medina's people and neighboring Bedouins must not remain behind or prefer themselves to the Messenger; the ayah directly forbids self-preserving withdrawal from shared struggle.

luna: The next ayah records every small or large expenditure and every valley crossed for the campaign; it makes the section's gift and completed action count even without naming victory. | terra: Every expenditure, small or great, and every valley crossed is recorded for reward; both giving and the physical completion of the march count as parts of the campaign.

luna: This ayah says believers should not all go forth together and describes a group learning and warning others; it is a limited boundary to 9:120's wartime call, since the exact division of who travels and who stays is not wholly clear from memory.

terra: The governor's wife gives each woman a knife and they cut their hands; the ayah concretely combines a blade handed to another person with the cutting action that distinguishes the section's effective sword.
terra: Abraham asks وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ; the same causative root means being kept away from danger, clarifying the protective force heard in سَيُجَنَّبُهَا.
terra: وَسَرَٰبِيلَ تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ names garments that protect people from their own violence, directly matching the shield's protective function in battle.
terra: The woman who unravels her yarn after it was strong figures covenant-breaking as undoing completed work; it is a nonmilitary counterpart to the attack begun and then abandoned.
terra: مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ receives good life and reward on the same condition of faith, separating natural sex from the dictionary's grading of iron.
terra: Servants أُو۟لِى بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ range through the dwellings when the promised judgment arrives; it stages the severe, effective assault named abstractly with iron in 57:25.
terra: قُلْ كُونُوا۟ حِجَارَةً أَوْ حَدِيدًا invokes iron as the imagined extreme of resistant hardness, supporting the physical quality behind the dictionary's hard iron.
luna: When given favor, a person turns away and draws aside with his flank (بِجَانِبِهِ); this repeats the source root ج ن ب's side image alongside the turn-away stance of the self-sufficient man.
terra: Zulqarnayn uses blocks of iron, heats them, and pours molten copper over them to make a barrier; hard metal here serves construction and defense rather than a cutting assault.
terra: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ states that the Godfearing are rescued while wrongdoers remain kneeling in Hell, directly matching the shield-like protection of the source's ٱلْأَتْقَى.
terra: The revealed warning ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the source sequence exactly: denial followed by turning away leads to punishment.

luna: This ayah says God taught David to make armor protecting people from their violence; it repeats the shield side of the section's image in an explicit battle setting. | terra: God teaches David the craft of armor لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ; it supplies the Quranic protective weapon for the section's shield kept at a fighter's side.
terra: Those for whom ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ has preceded are عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ from Hell; fair outcome and being kept away from fire converge just as ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ and سَيُجَنَّبُهَا do in the source image.
terra: Those kept far from Hell in 21:101 do not hear even its faint sound; this describes how complete the shield-like separation from fire is.

luna: The section's hard iron is a weapon in battle; this ayah places iron maces (مَقَامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ) in the Fire, turning the metal into punishment for those who rejected the truth. | terra: مَقَٰمِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍۢ supplies an explicit iron striking weapon, though it belongs to Hell's punishment rather than a human battlefield.
terra: Permission to fight is granted to those attacked and wronged, with a promise that God can give victory; the ayah joins justified combat to its hoped-for favorable end.
terra: Those driven from their homes are defended because unchecked aggression would destroy houses of worship; it supplies the protective purpose of the fighting permitted in 22:39.

luna: The verse names those who migrate in Allah's cause and are killed or die, then promises good provision and a pleasing entry; it develops the section's martyr outcome after combat. | terra: Those who emigrate and are then killed or die receive رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا; the good provision makes death in committed service an attained good rather than a failed campaign.
terra: They say they believe and obey, ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّىٰ فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنْهُم; the ayah directly measures a verbal profession by the action that turns away from it.
terra: When summoned to God's and the Messenger's judgment, a group is مُعْرِضُونَ; this supplies the concrete act behind the verbal-then-bodily turning of 24:47.
terra: True believers answer سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا when summoned to judgment; enacted obedience is the positive counterpart to the turners in 24:47-48.
terra: The queen's advisers declare themselves possessors of strength and severe might while leaving command to her; the ayah explicitly frames martial hardness as capacity awaiting a decision.

terra: The queen answers that kings ruin towns and abase their honored people when they enter; it supplies the destructive human consequence that limits admiration of the severe force claimed in 27:33.

terra: Moses' sister observes him عَن جُنُبٍۢ, using the root for a position off to the side or at a distance; the precise spatial nuance is uncertain, but it belongs to the sense underlying the shield's name.

luna: The source root ج ن ب names the shield at a person's side and being kept aside from fire; this ayah speaks of worshippers' sides (جُنُوبُهُمْ) leaving their beds as they call on God in fear and hope and give from their provision.

luna: During the same siege, some say Allah and His Messenger promised only delusion; this is the battlefield denial set against the pledge-fulfillment of 33:23 and the source section's broken charge. | terra: During the siege, hypocrites call God's and the Messenger's promise delusion; their denial under pressure is the negative counterpart to the believers' وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ in 33:22.

luna: Under siege, some tell the people to return and claim their homes are exposed; the verse says they want only to flee, making the source section's turn-away an explicit wartime retreat. | terra: During the siege some claim their houses are exposed, though God says they only intend flight; a spoken excuse masks the bodily retreat that the image treats as lying in action.

luna: Still within the siege, the verse says the wavering group would comply if attackers pressed them toward fitna; it shows their charge failing under pressure. | terra: Had the city been breached from its sides and treachery requested, the fearful would have yielded quickly; the ayah tests their firmness at the imagined point of enemy entry.

luna: The verse recalls their covenant not to turn backs (لَا يُوَلُّونَ الْأَدْبَارَ); the source section's root و ل ي names the opposing act of turning away in battle. | terra: The besieged had covenanted لَا يُوَلُّونَ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ; not turning backs is explicitly a promise to be fulfilled under attack, joining the section's truth and retreat roots.

luna: The verse says flight cannot help against death or killing; it makes the section's retreat a futile answer to battlefield danger. | terra: Flight from death or killing will not benefit the besieged; it states the futility of the battlefield escape whose broken covenant is named in 33:15.
luna: The verse asks who can protect them from Allah if harm is decreed; after 33:16's futile flight, it supplies the limit of the shield or bodily protection named in the section.

luna: The verse identifies those who hinder fighters, urge their brothers back, come to battle only a little, and are stingy; it concretizes the section's contrast between giving into the fight and breaking off. | terra: God knows the obstructionists who summon others away and come to battle only a little; partial attendance without committed fighting is the section's interrupted action.

luna: The fearful men are stingy during danger but use sharp tongues (أَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ) after fear passes; by analogy, it contrasts verbal sharpness with the section's effective, sustained weapon action. | terra: At danger the hypocrites reel in fear, but afterward assail believers بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ while begrudging good; their only sharp weapon is the tongue, exposing hard speech without battlefield courage or giving.

luna: The continuation says that if the confederates returned, these people would fight only a little; it completes 33:18's picture of those who barely enter battle. | terra: If the confederates return, the fearful wish to be among desert Arabs merely asking for news and would fight only a little; distance and token action expose their failed commitment.

luna: When believers see the Confederates, they say this is what Allah and His Messenger promised and that Allah and His Messenger spoke truly (وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ); this is the opposite battlefield stance to the deniers in 33:12. | terra: At the sight of the confederates the believers say وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ and increase in submission; 33:23 then shows that affirmed truth embodied in their own kept covenant.

luna: The root ص د ق in the source section means carrying a battle effort through; here, amid the Confederates' siege, men have fulfilled the covenant they made with Allah. | terra: Men who صَدَقُوا۟ مَا عَٰهَدُوا۟ include one who has fulfilled his vow and one still waiting without changing; truth is steadfast completion inside battle exactly as the section describes.

luna: The next ayah says Allah will reward the truthful for their truth (الصَّادِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ) and deal with hypocrites; it states the outcome of the fulfilled covenant in 33:23. | terra: لِّيَجْزِىَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ states the outcome of the battlefield fidelity in 33:22-23, completing the link between a sound charge and its reward.

luna: The continuation says Allah sent the disbelievers back in rage without gain and spared the believers battle; it supplies the enemy's retreat as a battlefield reversal after the faithful stance in 33:23. | terra: God turns the attacking disbelievers back without gain and spares believers the fighting; it supplies a divinely achieved victory outcome while showing that completion need not mean endless human attack.
terra: The paired men and women include ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ and ٱلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلْمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ; sex, truth, and giving meet without making female action weaker.

luna: The source section calls masculine iron the hardest; here Allah softens iron for David (وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ), a specific reversal showing iron can be made yielding for a different use. | terra: وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ makes iron pliant for David, a precise reversal of the dictionary's hardest male iron; 34:11 shows that softness enables protective armor rather than ineffective action.

luna: The next ayah turns the softened iron of 34:10 into coats of mail and asks for measured links; it gives the section's iron and shield image a Quranic defensive use. | terra: David is commanded to make full coats of mail and measure their links; the softened iron of 34:10 becomes effective protection, setting a boundary on the section's equation of soft metal with weak work.
terra: The son tells Abraham to do what he is commanded and promises patient endurance; his spoken assent deliberately commits him to the costly act begun in 37:103.
terra: Father and son submit and the son is laid down for sacrifice; this enacted submission is what 37:105 calls making the vision true.
terra: قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَا declares Abraham's vision made true after the submission staged in 37:102-103; truth here is accomplished action, not verbal assent.
luna: The source root ج ن ب also means to keep away: this ayah praises those who avoid false gods (اجْتَنَبُوا۟) and gives them good news, echoing the section's pious person kept away from fire.

terra: The one who brings truth and confirms it is identified with the Godfearing; the ayah joins صِدْق and taqwa, the same two qualities embodied by the source's truthful giver and protected fighter.
terra: God rescues those who feared Him and لَا يَمَسُّهُمُ ٱلسُّوٓءُ; this gives the theological reality represented by the section's shield beside the protected person.

terra: Whoever acts righteously, male or female, enters the Garden and is provided for without measure; action and outcome apply equally across the sex pair, limiting the old weapon terminology's strong/weak gender metaphor.
luna: This ayah repeats the person who turns aside with his flank after favor (بِجَانِبِهِ); the recurring side-image gives the source section's shield-at-the-flank dictionary sense a contrary use.
terra: God يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَٰثًۭا and يَهَبُ male children, bringing divine giving and the female/male pair into one ayah without the weapon lexicon's hierarchy.
terra: God may pair offspring ذُكْرَانًۭا وَإِنَٰثًۭا or make one barren; following 42:49, the pairing remains wholly governed by His gift.

luna: When armies meet, this verse describes striking necks before regulating captives; it supplies a concrete Quranic battle scene for the source section's cutting sword. | terra: At encounter, the command proceeds from striking necks حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَثْخَنتُمُوهُمْ to binding captives and until war lays down its burdens; it stages a cutting weapon and an assault carried to its defined end.

luna: This ayah promises help and firm feet to those who support Allah; it names the steadiness in battle that the section embodies through a sound spear and completed charge. | terra: God promises to support those who support His cause and وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ; firm feet are the bodily opposite of the retreating back.
luna: When a fighting passage is revealed, the sick-hearted look at the Messenger as if overcome by death; this gives the source section's failed charge a specific image of fear.

luna: The source root ص د ق names giving battle its due; this ayah says that after a decision, being true to Allah would be better, while 47:20 shows the fearful response when fighting is mentioned. | terra: When fighting has been mentioned in 47:20 and the matter becomes resolved, فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ would mean carrying obedience through; this is the section's claim that truth appears at the point of committed action.

luna: The command not to weaken or call for peace while superior (وَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ وَتَدْعُوا۟ إِلَى السَّلْمِ) directly sets a boundary against stopping an ongoing battle effort. | terra: فَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ وَتَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلسَّلْمِ forbids losing resolve while believers have the upper hand, closely matching the section's charge that must not be abandoned.

luna: The ayah calls people to spend in Allah's cause, names those who withhold, then says turning away (تَتَوَلَّوْا) brings replacement; it joins the source section's giving and turning-away roots to support for the fight. | terra: People are summoned to spend in God's way, but some are stingy, and the ayah then warns وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْا۟; withholding and turning away meet here exactly as the source opposes giving to retreat.

luna: At the pledge under the tree, the verse says whoever fulfills his covenant with Allah receives a great reward; it parallels the source section's completed charge as faithful action. | terra: The pledge is a pledge to God: one who breaks it harms himself, while whoever fulfills his covenant receives immense reward; this directly defines truth as carrying pledged action through.
terra: The Bedouin laggards plead that property and family occupied them, saying with tongues what is absent from hearts; campaign absence makes their speech false in action.
terra: Laggards who missed the hard expedition ask to follow when spoils are available; their selective willingness exposes words and action governed by gain rather than faithful resolve.

luna: Those left behind are called to fight a powerful people; obedience brings a good reward, while turning away brings punishment, joining combat participation to consequence. | terra: The laggards will be summoned against أُو۟لِى بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ and must fight or face surrender; وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْا۟ threatens the renewed retreat that the section opposes to a completed charge.
terra: God is pleased with the believers pledging under the tree, knows what is in their hearts, and rewards them with a near victory; inward truth, binding action, and conquest converge.

luna: If the disbelievers had fought the believers, they would have turned their backs; it gives the source section's retreat a clear reversal, with the enemy rather than the believer fleeing. | terra: Had the disbelievers fought, لَوَلَّوُا۟ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ; the root is staged as battlefield rout, the direct opposite of carrying an assault through.
terra: لَقَدْ صَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ ٱلرُّءْيَا بِٱلْحَقِّ is realized in secure entry and a near conquest; truth is shown becoming historical action and victory.

luna: By analogy only, the companions are severe toward disbelievers and merciful among themselves; that contrast resembles the section's hard and yielding materials, though this is not a weapons scene. | terra: أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ gives firmness and mercy their proper objects; it keeps the section's hard/soft contrast from becoming a claim that hardness is always superior.
terra: Creation مِن ذَكَرٍۢ وَأُنثَىٰ leads to the criterion إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ; piety, not the section's figurative hard/soft gender names, sets human worth.

luna: This ayah calls those who believe without doubt and strive with wealth and lives in Allah's cause the truthful (الصَّادِقُونَ); it directly joins the source root ص د ق to completed combat action. | terra: Striving with wealth and lives is the evidence for أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ; the ayah explicitly identifies truth with enacted expenditure and struggle.
terra: فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌۭ uses the iron root adjectivally for sharp sight, preserving the sharpness component heard in the section's hard, cutting iron while changing the object entirely.
terra: قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ names the bow as a measure of nearness rather than as a fired weapon; it preserves the section's bow object while showing a different Quranic use.

terra: أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ introduces a man whose turning away is immediately specified by 53:34 as giving a little and stopping, nearly an exact nonmilitary enactment of the section's aborted charge.
terra: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًۭا وَأَكْدَىٰ joins the section's giving verb to an action cut short; 53:33 supplies the man's prior تَوَلَّىٰ, so the pair makes incomplete giving itself a retreat.

terra: وَأَنَّهُۥ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ repeats the source's created male/female pair, anchoring the weapon terms in the primary biological sense from which the dictionary metaphor departs.
terra: سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ predicts a host routed and turning its back, a compact counterpart to the section's flight scene.

luna: This ayah places spending and fighting before or after the conquest under one promise of الْحُسْنَىٰ, joining the section's given hand and sustained battle to a promised good. | terra: Spending and fighting before the conquest stand together, and وَكُلًّۭا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ; this is the section's explicit junction of giving, completed combat, and the fair outcome.
terra: ٱلْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَٱلْمُصَّدِّقَٰتِ pairs charitable men and women under one multiplied reward, joining the sex pair to the giving branch of the same صدق root.

luna: The section's dictionary scene makes iron the hardest metal and sharp sword material; this ayah says iron holds formidable power and benefits for people, connecting the weapon metal to strength used in support of God's messengers. | terra: Iron is sent down فِيهِ بَأْسٌۭ شَدِيدٌۭ; its severe martial force is the most direct Quranic counterpart to the section's hard iron made into an effective weapon.

luna: The source section names a shield as a side-protector; here oaths are made a shield (جُنَّة) that blocks people from Allah's path, a reversed and figurative use of protection rather than the same root.

luna: The connection is thematic, not a battle scene: the next ayah says wealth and children cannot avail the people just described and assigns them to the Fire, echoing the source section's wider surah context where wealth fails and fire follows denial.
luna: The hypocrites promise to leave with their allies or help them if attacked, but Allah calls them liars (لَكَاذِبُونَ); this is the source root ك ذ ب applied to a broken battle pledge.

luna: The next ayah says the hypocrites will not leave or help if their allies are attacked, then will turn their backs; it spells out the failure forecast in 59:11. | terra: The hypocrites promise support, yet if their allies are fought they will not help, and if they do help لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ; false assurance ends in the section's back-turning.
terra: بَأْسُهُم بَيْنَهُمْ شَدِيدٌۭ sounds like severe force, yet their hearts are divided; the ayah warns that outward hardness without inward cohesion is not the section's sound charge.
terra: Satan tells a person to disbelieve and then, once he does, disowns him; incitement followed by abandonment is a nonmilitary parallel to urging an action and failing it at the decisive point.

luna: The rebuke asks why people say what they do not do; the next battle image in 61:4 carries the source section's point about completing an action beyond verbal affirmation. | terra: لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ rebukes the split between assertion and action; 61:4 supplies the battle line in which words must become steadfast deed.

luna: This ayah says Allah greatly detests saying what one does not do; its battlefield neighbor 61:4 turns the source section's speech/action contrast into a fighting formation. | terra: The divine abhorrence of saying what one does not do sharpens the section's distinction between verbal assent and carrying the act through; 61:4 immediately stages the positive form in battle.

luna: The fighters stand as a compact structure (بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ); the source section's dictionary gloss of ص د ق as solid becomes a formation, not only hard iron. | terra: God loves those who fight in a rank كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَٰنٌۭ مَّرْصُوصٌۭ; the compact, solid line is the Quranic scene closest to the section's hard metal and sound, sustained assault.
luna: The ayah opens with a trade that saves from painful punishment; the next verse defines that trade as belief and striving with wealth and lives, echoing the section's gift-and-battle exchange.

luna: The verse defines the saving trade as believing in Allah and His Messenger and striving with wealth and lives; it states the section's giving and combat effort in one proposition. | terra: Striving with wealth and selves makes belief into expenditure and struggle; 61:12-13 then divide its beloved result into the next-world reward and near victory.

luna: The next ayah promises forgiveness, gardens, and a good dwelling for the fighters of 61:11; it supplies the afterlife reward alongside the section's victory-or-martyrdom outcome. | terra: Forgiveness and gardens are the enduring outcome of the striving in 61:11; paired with the worldly victory of 61:13, they illuminate the section's two fair outcomes.

luna: The ayah adds a nearer victory and conquest believers love (نَصْرٌ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ); after 61:11's spending and striving, it gives a concrete victory-side outcome. | terra: نَصْرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌۭ قَرِيبٌۭ is the other desired good beside 61:12's gardens, giving victory as the present-world partner of promised reward.

luna: The section's shield is physical protection, while this ayah makes oaths a shield (جُنَّة) for people who obstruct Allah's path; the connection is a specific metaphorical reversal, not a shared root.
luna: Outside a battle scene, the next ayah says these people believed and then disbelieved; it follows the false shield in 63:2 and parallels the source section's denier who turns away.
terra: Fear God as able, listen, obey, and spend; the sequence makes giving part of enacted obedience and distinguishes human limitation from refusal.
terra: قُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًۭا commands active protection from fire, the moral action rendered visible by the section's shield.

luna: This ayah says the Fire calls whoever turned away (تَوَلَّىٰ); it echoes the source root و ل ي and makes the section's back-turning lead directly toward its warned fire. | terra: The blazing fire تَدْعُوا۟ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ; it directly joins turning away with the fire that awaits the denier in the source, while 70:15 identifies that fire.
luna: The next ayah describes that person as one who gathered and hoarded (فَأَوْعَىٰ); it completes 70:17's picture of the one called by the Fire and opposes the section's giver who hands over.
terra: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ makes the rejecter's inward arrogance bodily as a turned back; 74:26 then gives his fire-bound end.
terra: سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ is the destination of the man who turned back in 74:23, repeating the source movement from rejection and withdrawal to fire.
terra: وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the source's two verbs in the same order, making denial issue in bodily departure.
terra: فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ again grounds the two weapon labels in the Quranic pair of created sexes.
terra: They give food despite loving it to the needy, orphan, and captive; 76:9-11 show this gift completed without repayment and answered by divine protection.
terra: The givers seek God's face alone and want neither recompense nor thanks, making the gift a fully carried act rather than an exchange left awaiting return.
terra: Their fear of a grim day supplies the Godfearing motive behind the giving of 76:8 and the protective outcome of 76:11.
terra: فَوَقَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمِ makes protection the answer to the fearful, selfless giving of 76:8-10, closely matching the source's shielded giver.
terra: Pharaoh فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَىٰ rejects and disobeys; 79:22 turns that refusal into bodily withdrawal and renewed hostile action.

terra: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ follows denial with turning back and active striving against Moses, paralleling the source sequence while showing that retreat from truth can still be energetic opposition.

terra: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَشْقَى reverses the source relation: the wretched one avoids the reminder, whereas in the source the most Godfearing is made to avoid the fire; 87:12 gives the consequence.
terra: The wretched person who avoids the reminder in 87:11 يَصْلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ; avoiding the warning leads into fire, opposite the pious person's being kept from it.
terra: The one who تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ is singled out for the greatest punishment in 88:24, a close semantic parallel to denial, turning, and fire in the source.
terra: فَيُعَذِّبُهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَكْبَرَ supplies the consequence for the turning unbeliever of 88:23, completing that parallel to the source warning.
terra: أَرَءَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the same denial-and-turning pair while the surrounding scene concerns a man obstructing prayer.
terra: The panting chargers open a sustained cavalry assault; their forward exertion gives the section's completed charge a direct Quranic scene without relying on shared vocabulary.
terra: The chargers strike sparks from the ground, contributing the hard impact of weapon-like force to the assault begun in 100:1.
terra: The horses raid at dawn, identifying the preceding motion as an actual attack rather than general travel.
terra: The charge raises a cloud of dust, making the speed and physical force of the advance visible.
terra: The chargers penetrate into the midst of a gathered force, bringing the sequence's attack all the way to its objective and thus closely enacting the section's sound charge.
